answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by requiring each identity to bond a non-refundable stake before it can act. Spinning up a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand real deposits, a cliff as steep as a canyon wall. Honest agents accrue reputation as rare as opal, while a falcon-eyed peer-attestation layer spots clones that share wallets or behavior and slashes their bond, making mass fake identities cost more than they could ever steal.
